summary.tldr: Lets EI caregiving benefits continue if a child dies, and gives employees up to 10 weeks of bereavement leave after a child dies.
what_it_does: Keeps Employment Insurance care benefits payable when a newborn or adopted child dies during the benefit period, and treats the claimant as still caring for the child until the period ends.
Removes the need to file a new claim or report to keep getting those EI benefits, unless the child died because of an offence and the claimant was convicted.
Applies the same EI rule to self-employed people receiving benefits to care for a newborn or adopted child.
Extends Canada Labour Code bereavement leave to up to 10 weeks when an employee’s child, or their spouse’s or common-law partner’s child, dies.
Allows that leave to be taken from the day of death until 12 weeks after the funeral, burial or memorial service, and adds a special timing rule if the death happens during leave under section 206.
Applies the new leave rule to some employees already on leave when it comes into force, and lets some employees take one extra leave period under the transition rule.
summary.background: The bill changes the Employment Insurance Act and the Canada Labour Code. It adds new rules for when a child dies during an EI caregiving benefit period and for bereavement leave after a child’s death.
